reviews.review:
After playing through the first episode, I wish there were a neutral review option for this one.

I really like the idea of this episode taking place years after the amazing ending of the first episode, with Hal still carrying the weight of his failure, but I feel like all of the things that made the latter half of the first episode great were not present in this one. 
First, the development of the connection between Hal and Chris/Eleanor. Despite there being a large emphasis of the beginning and the ending towards Chris, honestly I could not give a shit about her. She wasn't interesting in the first episode given that she wasn't a main character, and, from the readers perspective, all of a sudden she's the star of Hal's life, even if it was just the sense of duty to pay her back on his end. Really, it would have been better if there was some sort of flashback or continuation of the first episode where it shows Chris and Hal becoming closer. Chris also never does anything in this episode, she just talks to Hal, cries, reminds Hal of Hagana and his past failure, and is generally just useless in terms of moving the plot forward. As for Eleanor, I honestly liked her character from the moment her motivations were revealed to the ending, she does draw a lot of parallels to Hagana, but that's also what I thought made Hagana a good character in the first episode; she wants a sense of purpose and justice in the cruel state of their lives, and when given the opportunity to make a difference, both of them went to an extreme to do so. Despite that, she isn't just a stand-in for Hagana, she has more extreme ways of moving toward her goal, and connected with Hal through wanting to achieve her dream rather than not wanting to be worthless.
Second, the ending felt so disappointing compared to the first episode. I loved the ending of the first episode because it could stand alone as an ending, even if there were no other episodes, or it could lead into the next chapter of Hal's life. This ending is purely just a cliffhanger, and it felt very abrupt. Its very explicitly stated what the plan of action is to take down Avalon, even Chris seems to finally have some story significance after her confession to Hal, but then the episode just ends? Just an overall very unsatisfying ending.
Finally, there just seems to be so many plot threads that lead absolutely nowhere. The whole company thing with Le Goff and Marco is just forgotten halfway through the story in exchange for the war on Avalon, and is never brought up again. Eleanor praying at the church is not brought up again past the initial moment they talk about it. Hal's talk about God and faith with Lisa nearing the end also isn't used after the initial conversation, even though it felt like a turning point within Hal's subconscious. Everything with Rena just felt completely pointless after Hal leaves the government job, and even the one moment that Rena actually contributed to the plot felt like that moment was the whole purpose of her character, to just exist to feed extremely convenient information to Hal, then to permanently fuck off. She really couldn't have had a bigger role in starting the downfall of Avalon? She's literally a government worker, do something with that? Lastly, the talk with Toyama and analysts. That whole talk feels really meaningless if we are never told what Eleanor had to go through as an analyst for the top investment banking company on the entire Moon, other than that Eleanor had to abuse drugs to go to sleep. What was she treated like within the banking company? How much time did she spend actually being an analyst? Was her pay worth the suffering? Did acting as Susie Wu seep into her actual life?

I know this episode is probably just build up and development to the third episode, but it really should be able to stand alone like the first episode did. I loved the first episode, but this one just isn't anywhere near as good as the first. 5/10
